accuracy.evidence: The age claim matches the CDC 2022 milestone wording for 2 years (says at least two words together, like More milk); the meaning groups follow Brown's 1973 stage I relations (recurrence more, nonexistence all gone, rejection no, agent plus action dog run, possessor plus possession Daddy shoe, entity plus location teddy bed, attribute big ball); the say-it-back advice is the recast or expansion step supported by the Cleave et al. 2015 meta-analysis. No claim that telegraphic speech is wrong.

misconceptions.evidence: Child slips: one word when two would say more (milk), a word that does not fit the picture (more car, baby run, teddy bed when teddy is in the box) and the wrong order (milk more, fly bird). Grown-up slips named in the adult text and targeted in step 5 and the challenge: demanding the whole sentence, replying with no words, and a reply far too long to copy.

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab is built from two-word slots: word cards drop into word 1 and word 2 under an empty cup, a running dog or a car driving away; a shoe, a sock and a hat are dragged to the person wearing the matching one to make Daddy shoe; then a child speech bubble gets a grown-up reply and grows to three words. It teaches word combining and recasts only, not sentences or vocabulary.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers that a card has to fit the picture and the slot order (the reply says there is no car here, or we say more first), that ownership is shown by the matching item, and in step 5 that the recast reply makes the child bubble grow from big dog to big dog run; the step text confirms each meaning after the task.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong answers: a second word adds nothing (the cup round shows more milk says what is wanted), teddy bed is wrong because it lacks in the (the step shows two words is the stage, with no correction), and asking for the whole sentence helps most (step 5 shows a recast gets more words from the child, while fix gets a reply that it stops the talk).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Eight challenge questions; every wrong option carries a tag with its own reply: one (add a second word), fit (that word does not fit the picture), order (say it the way grown-ups do), fix (asking for the whole sentence can stop the talk), flat (no words back gives nothing to copy) and long (too long to copy).

readability.evidence: Kid text is short sentences of one-syllable words such as more milk, all gone and bye car, FK well under the family kid target; adult text reads at FK 6.5 and explains the key words two-word phrase, word combination, expansion and recast.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs each give one kind of two-word phrase (wanting more, all gone and bye, who and what, whose and where); adult paragraphs give the milestone, the meaning groups with examples, the grown-up and child slips, and what each lab step does, with nothing repeated.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark: word cards are 2 by 2 with large picture and word, the two slots sit under the scene, the three people fit one row, the speech bubbles stack beside a small scene in step 5, the tray buttons are full size and nothing is clipped at 390 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a tray button (say the word, give the hat to Gran, say back a reply); the canvas aria-label is rewritten after every reply; text on filled cards and owner boxes uses light ink on dark green in the dark theme; walk.cjs runs axe in both themes on desktop and phone.

sources: CDC Learn the Signs. Act Early. Milestones (revised 2022): 2 years, says at least two words together, like More milk
DfE Development Matters (2021): Communication and Language, birth to three
Brown, R. (1973) A First Language: The Early Stages. Harvard University Press (stage I semantic relations)

Cleave, P. L., Becker, S. D., Curran, M. K., Owen Van Horne, A. J. and Fey, M. E. (2015) The efficacy of recasts in language intervention: a systematic review and meta-analysis. American Journal of Speech-Language Pathology 24(2)
